clue.text: Put in the box for having reconnoitred a burglary

definitions.meaning: packed into a case or container
to case a joint is criminal slang for inspecting it before a break-in

explanation.surface: A burglar is jailed for having scouted the premises beforehand.
explanation.definitionFit: Packed in a container, and also the past tense of slang for scouting a target before a robbery.

clue.text: Use snow plough only if there is no traffic ahead

definitions.meaning: to clear the road of snow

definitions.text: only if there is no traffic ahead
definitions.meaning: an open route with nothing in front

explanation.surface: Advice to drive a snow plough only when the way in front is empty.
explanation.definitionFit: Ploughing clears a highway; and an empty highway in front of a driver is an unobstructed route.

clue.text: What old boy can't assume unless he is collared

definitions.text: What old boy can't assume unless he is collared

parts.words: What old boy can't assume unless he is collared
parts.note: a former pupil can only put on his alma mater's neckwear if he wears a collar; collared also suggests arrested

explanation.surface: Something a former pupil can't take on unless he is arrested.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old boy' means a former pupil, and 'collared' looks like arrested but means wearing a shirt collar to knot neckwear round.
explanation.definitionFit: Former pupils wear their alma mater's striped neckwear, a symbol of the old-boy network.

clue.text: Mild expletive to replace an unprintable one

definitions.meaning: a gentle oath like 'drat'
printers put a line in place of a swear word, as in d---

explanation.surface: A gentle curse used instead of a rude one.
explanation.definitionFit: 'Drat it' style softened oath; also the printed line standing in for the letters of a rude word.

clue.text: Ice is not the most pleasant to wash in

definitions.meaning: frozen liquid is literally solid, rigid stuff from the tap

definitions.text: not the most pleasant to wash in
definitions.meaning: water rich in lime makes poor lather and leaves scum

explanation.surface: Bathing in ice is hardly the nicest way to get clean.
explanation.definitionFit: Ice is solid, so jokingly firm liquid; and limescale-laden supply lathers badly, so washing in it is unpleasant.

clue.text: Farrier knows how to make one awkward corner

definitions.text: Farrier knows how to make one
definitions.meaning: a blacksmith shapes U-shaped iron plates for hooves
a tight U-shaped curve in a road or river

explanation.surface: A blacksmith can produce an awkward corner.
explanation.definitionFit: A farrier curves iron for hooves; a road or river looping back on itself in a U-shape is named after that iron.

clue.text: It sounds like questions to men of learning

indicators.note: signals that the word is heard rather than read

parts.note: whys are questions asking for reasons

explanation.surface: Something resembling queries put to scholars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Men of learning' points to the Wise Men; the definition is 'of learning', i.e. knowledgeable.
explanation.definitionFit: Learned and sagacious; knowledgeable people are called sages.

clue.text: Where the Roman tribe settled

indicators.note: the letters of tribe are settled into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: The place an ancient Roman people made their home.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition reads loosely: the river where the Roman (tribe) settled.
explanation.definitionFit: The river flowing through Rome, beside which the city was founded.

clue.text: Egyptian deity born to be an Indian queen

parts.note: Ra was the Egyptian sun god
née marks a woman's maiden name

explanation.surface: An Egyptian god's daughter is destined to rule in India.
explanation.definitionFit: A rajah's wife or a Hindu princess ruling in her own right.

clue.text: Those forming the character of a society

indicators.note: the letters of the first word are formed into a new shape

explanation.surface: Certain people shape what a society is like.
explanation.definitionFit: An ethos is the distinctive spirit, beliefs and values of a group or culture.

clue.text: Don't accept a lot of wine only for disposal

parts.note: to refuse is to turn down
a bin is a cellar rack holding a stock of bottles, as in a wine bin

explanation.surface: Someone rejects a whole stock of wine and simply throws it away.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is loose: a container meant for rubbish disposal.
explanation.definitionFit: A rubbish receptacle is the thing used for getting rid of waste.

clue.text: Maybe that imp Ariel is an enthusiast for keeping windows open

definitions.meaning: Ariel in The Tempest is a sprite of the air, an airy demon

definitions.text: an enthusiast for keeping windows open
definitions.meaning: someone who loves ventilation

explanation.surface: Shakespeare's sprite is a fan of ventilated rooms.
explanation.walkthrough: Ariel is a cheeky (fresh) spirit of the air, an imp or fiend, so literally a lively 'air fiend'.
explanation.definitionFit: Ariel, Prospero's impish air spirit, is cheeky and airy; and the phrase means a ventilation fanatic.

clue.text: Screen covering

definitions.meaning: a ... screen is the carved partition between nave and chancel in a church
an old unit of land area, a quarter of an acre, is the ground a field covers

explanation.surface: A screen that hides something from view.
explanation.definitionFit: A crucifix above a church's chancel screen gives that screen its name; it is also a quarter-acre measure of land.

clue.text: It's even. But wouldn't be if it is removed

definitions.text: It's even. But wouldn't be if it is removed

parts.note: the 's of the contraction supplies a single sibilant letter

explanation.surface: A puzzling remark about a quantity that is level only until something is taken away.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'It's even' literally: an S followed by EVEN. The whole clue is the riddle: the number is odd, but take that S away and what is left says even.
explanation.definitionFit: Six plus one is an odd number, yet its spelling ends in the word for divisible by two.

clue.text: Release from prison if there is no charge

definitions.meaning: to let a captive go
costing nothing, gratis

explanation.surface: A prisoner is let out because no charge has been brought.
explanation.definitionFit: To liberate someone, and also costing nothing at all.

clue.text: Head off squash and overrule one's conviction

indicators.note: the first letter of squash is cut away

explanation.surface: Someone stops a squash match and overturns a guilty verdict.
explanation.definitionFit: A court annuls a verdict by setting it aside.

clue.text: Going into the movies Henry shows backbone

parts.note: cine refers to cinema or film
H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance

explanation.surface: A man named Henry shows courage by going to the cinema.
explanation.definitionFit: A cut of meat along the spine, or an animal's backbone itself.

clue.text: How Americans swear to arouse sympathy

definitions.meaning: US citizens pledge allegiance with a hand placed on the chest
to move someone emotionally

explanation.surface: The way people in the USA take an oath stirs our feelings.
explanation.walkthrough: Americans reciting the Pledge of Allegiance put their right hand over the left side of the chest.
explanation.definitionFit: Placing a hand on the chest is the US oath gesture; figuratively the phrase means to move someone deeply.

clue.text: Somewhere to hold your breath when the air liner hits it?

definitions.text: Somewhere to hold your breath when the air liner hits it?

parts.words: Somewhere to hold your breath when the air liner hits it?
parts.note: a downdraught makes a plane drop suddenly, so nervous fliers gasp; also a bubble where a trapped person can breathe

explanation.surface: A place where passengers gasp as their plane strikes turbulence.
explanation.definitionFit: A region of thin or downward-moving atmosphere causing an aircraft to drop sharply.

clue.text: No short requisition is a difficult undertaking

parts.note: not short means of great height

explanation.surface: A large request for supplies is hard to fulfil.
explanation.definitionFit: An unreasonably demanding task or request.

clue.text: One responsible for drawing up new female habits

definitions.text: One responsible for drawing up new female habits

parts.words: One responsible for drawing up new female habits
parts.note: habits looks like customs, but here means garments; drawing up means sketching patterns for women's clothes

explanation.surface: Someone who devises new behaviour patterns for women.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Habits' suggests ways of behaving (or a nun's robes); here it simply means clothes, and 'drawing up' means sketching them.
explanation.definitionFit: A couturier sketches and creates new garments, especially women's frocks.

clue.text: She is classy at heart

indicators.note: only the core of the word classy is used, dropping its outer letters

explanation.surface: A woman who is fundamentally stylish.
explanation.definitionFit: A girl or young woman, so a pronoun for a female can stand for her.

clue.text: Liberal, socially acceptable 'tecs are clear headed

parts.note: U means upper-class or acceptable, from the 'U and non-U' usage debate
the CID, Criminal Investigation Department, is the British police detective branch

explanation.surface: Respectable liberal detectives are sharp thinkers.
explanation.definitionFit: Thinking rationally and expressing oneself intelligibly.

clue.text: Police car warning an alluring female

definitions.meaning: the wailing alarm on an emergency vehicle
a seductive temptress, from the singing sea nymphs of myth

explanation.surface: A police car sounds a warning about a seductive woman.
explanation.definitionFit: The wailing alarm of emergency vehicles, and a seductive temptress like the sea nymphs of Greek myth.

clue.text: Brawny worker confronting a disheartened fly

parts.note: a worker bee is the standard crossword worker

indicators.note: the fly loses its heart, its central letter, leaving the outer pair

explanation.surface: A muscular labourer squares up to a dispirited insect.
explanation.definitionFit: Muscular and strongly built, as a big beefcake of a man is.

clue.text: Clown who appeared for two companies

indicators.note: two of the abbreviation are needed, one for each company

parts.note: CO is the standard abbreviation for company

explanation.surface: A circus clown worked for a pair of firms.
explanation.walkthrough: Coco was a famous circus clown in Britain (Nicolai Poliakoff of Bertram Mills Circus).
explanation.definitionFit: Coco the Clown was a celebrated Russian-born British circus performer.

clue.text: Language used for unnumbered verse

indicators.note: the Roman numeral five is removed from verse

explanation.surface: A tongue suited to poetry without numbered lines.
explanation.definitionFit: Irish or Scottish Gaelic, the Celtic tongue of the Highlands and Ireland.

clue.text: Crack a biscuit

definitions.meaning: to break suddenly with a sharp sound
a ginger ... is a crisp cookie

explanation.surface: Breaking a cookie in two.
explanation.definitionFit: Breaking with a sharp crack; also a thin crisp gingerbread cookie.

clue.text: Evidence of gun shot found between two farm track ruts?

definitions.meaning: the spent case left behind after a firearm is discharged

definitions.text: found between two farm track ruts?
definitions.meaning: the raised strip between wheel ruts on a cart track is a ...

explanation.surface: Proof that a gun was fired turns up on a farm lane.
explanation.definitionFit: A spent shell casing proves a shot was fired; and the hump between a wagon's wheel ruts is literally a cart ridge.

clue.text: Knead, knead, with bare skin

indicators.note: to knead is to work dough about, so the first word's letters are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: A baker kneads and kneads with bare arms.
explanation.definitionFit: Unclothed, with skin uncovered, is what nude or stripped means.

clue.text: Accompanists to a troupe of artistes?

definitions.text: Accompanists to a troupe of artistes?

parts.words: Accompanists to a troupe of artistes?
parts.note: musicians accompanying a troupe of performers; a band that plays for those who dance, read as a punning group

explanation.surface: The musicians who back up a touring company of performers.
explanation.walkthrough: The troupe suggests a group of dancers, so the musicians backing them are literally a band for dancing.
explanation.definitionFit: A group of musicians playing music for ballroom dancing.

clue.text: Father of the 'art for art's sake 'school

definitions.meaning: Latin for dad, a schoolboy word
Walter ... was the Victorian critic behind the aesthetic movement

explanation.surface: The founding figure of the Aesthetic movement.
explanation.walkthrough: Walter Pater (1839-94) was the English critic whose writing inspired Aestheticism's 'art for art's sake'.
explanation.definitionFit: Latin for dad, used in old public-school slang; and the surname of the Victorian aesthete critic Walter.
